From: Samira Khan <samira@healthgauge.ai>

Subject: Quick request: per-1M token baseline + model roster

Hi Aditya —

We are doing a sizing pass for an LLM-powered triage feature at HealthGauge and want to capture a baseline for hosted API economics. Could you send your standard per-1M token rates (input vs output split) and the short list of models you recommend for low-latency production (and approximate relative latency/QoS tiers)?

Also curious: do you have published discount bands for committed monthly tokens (examples: 5M, 20M, 100M)? If you could attach a one-page rate snapshot or link to a simple table that would be ideal — we’re collecting numbers to present to our procurement team next week.

We care about SOC2 and SSO (we may need a compliance checklist later) — high level is fine for now.

Thanks — can loop Tom in if you need more technical detail.

—Samira
VP Product, HealthGauge

Attachments: none
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khan <samira@healthgauge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick request: per-1M token baseline + model roster

Samira —

Thanks for the note. Attaching a one-page preview (HealthGauge-Ratecard-Preview.pdf) and a CSV with a compact pricing table. Below is a quick baseline snapshot for our hosted API (per 1M tokens):

- rw-instruct-7B: input $0.75 / 1M, output $1.80 / 1M — low-latency, cost-optimized for short prompts
- rw-chat-13B: input $1.60 / 1M, output $3.50 / 1M — good balance of quality and latency
- rw-mammoth-70B: input $5.20 / 1M, output $11.00 / 1M — highest quality, higher memory/latency profile
- open-eval-7B (community): input $0.50 / 1M, output $1.20 / 1M — lower-cost open model, best for non-sensitive tasks

Notes:
- Input vs output split: we bill separately for input tokens (prompt + system + function args) and output tokens (generated). Output token costs are typically higher because of compute and memory footprint.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: per-token math is the same; streaming simply changes latency characteristics.
- Function calls and tool outputs: any tokens generated by a tool call or function output are counted as output tokens.

Standard committed-discount bands (hosted API):
- 5M tokens/month: 10% off baseline
- 20M tokens/month: 15% off baseline + 30-day invoice terms
- 100M tokens/month: 22% off baseline + optional dedicated capacity evaluation
- Custom enterprise: >250M/month — bespoke pricing, extended SLAs, and dedicated onboarding

Compliance & procurement: we have a SOC 2 Type II package and SSO integrations (SAML/OIDC). I can share the checklist after we sign an NDA or via a secure link.

Would you like a short call to walk through which model is the best tradeoff for your triage workload (latency vs quality)? I’m available tomorrow 9–11am PT or Wednesday afternoon.

—Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: HealthGauge-Ratecard-Preview.pdf, single-page-pricing-table.csv

Thanks Aditya — quick clarifications: 

1) When you say "function calls and tool outputs" count as output tokens, does that include the returned JSON payload (we often post-process and include structured fields)?
2) Do you provide guidance on expected latency (p50/p95) for rw-chat-13B vs rw-mammoth-70B on hosted API? Our SLO target is p95 < 350ms for single-turn requests.
3) On the discount bands: is the 5M band a prepay or committed spend? Our procurement will ask whether discounts require committed monthly minimums vs annual commitments.

If you can add these points in your next note that would help speed procurement. If it's easier I can take the 30-min call — Tom (cc'd on the original) should join for latency/infra questions.

—Samira
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khan <samira@healthgauge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-13T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick request: per-1M token baseline + model roster

Samira —

Answers inline: 

1) Yes — any tokens returned in the HTTP response (including JSON payloads, function-returned text, metadata) are counted as output tokens. If you plan to generate large structured payloads, that will increase output-side costs; we can run a small sample to estimate token volumes.

2) Latency (hosted API, typical p50 / p95 under normal load):
- rw-instruct-7B: 60ms / 140ms
- rw-chat-13B: 120ms / 320ms (your p95 target of 350ms is achievable for single-turn; rw-chat-13B commonly meets p95 < 350ms with our hosting configuration)
- rw-mammoth-70B: 220ms / 760ms (high variance at p95; better for high-quality, multi-turn tasks where p95 <= 800ms is acceptable)

3) Discount logistics: the 5M band is a monthly committed volume (month-to-month credit against invoices) — you don't have to prepay the full year, but discounts apply only when the monthly committed threshold is met. Annual committed spend contracts can increase discount depth (we typically move from the monthly bands above to an additional ~5% for year-long commitments). We can provide contract language for both models.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share the compliance checklist link privately (contains SOC 2 summary and SSO integration guide).
- If you want, book a 30-minute session (I'll include Laura from Commercial Ops to go over contract terms). Suggested times: Apr 14, 10:00am PT or Apr 15, 2:00pm PT.

If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short sample estimate based on a 3M input / 6M output token monthly baseline using rw-chat-13B.

—Aditya
